html:
A court set up in 2002 by Sierra Leone and the United Nations to try those most responsible for crimes in the civil war, sitting in Freetown.

It was the first such court with both national and international judges, and the first to convict people of recruiting child soldiers and of forced marriage as a crime against humanity. It tried leaders of the RUF, the army junta and the pro-government militias. In 2012, sitting in The Hague for security, it convicted Charles Taylor, the first former head of state convicted by an international court since the Nuremberg trials. It closed in 2013.
sum: A court set up in 2002 by Sierra Leone and the United Nations to try those most responsible for crimes in the civil war, sitting in Freetown.
